record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: For a translationally invariant projected entangled pair state (PEPS) on an L by L torus defined by a local tensor A, let R be a square region and let H be the parent Hamiltonian obtained by translating the local projector associated to R. What are the weakest conditions on the tensor A, and how small can the region R be chosen, that guarantee the resulting PEPS is the unique ground state of H and that H has a nonzero spectral gap?

artifact.status_search_result: Uniqueness of the ground state is well understood under "injectivity" or "MPO-injectivity" conditions on the tensor, but proving the existence of a nonzero spectral gap for parent Hamiltonians of 2D PEPS is generally open. The problem is known to be undecidable for general PEPS, and even the gap of the simplest nontrivial AKLT-type model has only recently been established. Partial sufficient conditions (e.g., approximate factorization of boundary states, "locality at the boundary implies gap in the bulk") have been obtained, but the optimal/weakest conditions on $A$ and the smallest admissible region $R$ remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Locality at the Boundary Implies Gap in the Bulk for 2D PEPS
status_evidence.snippet: Approximate factorization of boundary states implies a constant gap of the bulk parent Hamiltonian.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a sufficient condition for the gap but not the optimal one.

status_evidence.title: PEPS as unique ground states of local Hamiltonians
status_evidence.snippet: Sufficient injectivity conditions yielding uniqueness of the PEPS as ground state of the parent Hamiltonian.
status_evidence.claim: Addresses uniqueness but not the gap question in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
status_evidence.snippet: Lists as an open question the determination of weakest conditions on A and the smallest region R guaranteeing uniqueness and gap.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly posed as open.
